title: Engraving Words on Plates
summary: Jacob says he has ministered much to his people but can write only a little because engraving words on plates is difficult. He says they labor diligently to engrave words on plates, hoping their children and beloved brethren will receive them with thankful hearts and learn with joy.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob has ministered much to his people in word.
Jacob says he can write only a little of his words because engraving words on plates is difficult.
Jacob says writings on plates remain, while writings on anything else perish and vanish away.
The words on plates can give their children and beloved brethren a small degree of knowledge concerning them or their fathers.
Jacob says they rejoice and labor diligently to engrave the words, hoping those readers receive them with thankful hearts and learn with joy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob engraving words on a plate.
unspecified_visual_details: The plate’s appearance, the engraving tool, Jacob’s appearance, and the setting.

narration.text: I cannot write but a little of my words
we can write a few words upon plates
we labor diligently to engraven these words upon plates

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The children and beloved brethren are hoped-for readers, not people shown receiving the plates in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict future readers receiving the plates or reacting to them.
Do not assign Jacob an age or invent the identities of others included in “we.”

title: Hope in Christ
summary: Jacob explains that the record testifies of their hope in Christ before his coming, the prophets' belief in Christ, worship of the Father in his name, and the law of Moses pointing souls to him.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says the writings are intended to show that he and his people knew of Christ and hoped for his glory before his coming.
Jacob says holy prophets before them also hoped for Christ's glory and believed in Christ.
Jacob says they worship the Father in Christ's name and keep the law of Moses because it points their souls to Christ.
Jacob refers to Abraham's obedience in offering Isaac in the wilderness as a similitude of God and his Only Begotten Son.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown speaking or writing as he teaches.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Jacob is speaking to an audience or writing during this teaching.

narration.text: they believed in Christ and worshiped the Father in his name
it pointing our souls to him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Abraham and Isaac are mentioned in a comparison; the verse does not narrate their offering as a present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Abraham offering Isaac as an event occurring in this scene.

title: Witnesses and faith
summary: Jacob says they search the prophets and have revelations and prophecy, obtaining hope and unshaken faith. He teaches that their power comes by the Lord God's grace and condescensions.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says they search the prophets and have many revelations and the spirit of prophecy.
Jacob says these witnesses give them hope and unshaken faith, and says they can command in Jesus's name and trees, mountains, or sea waves obey.
Jacob says the Lord God shows them their weakness so they know their power comes by God's grace and condescensions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown teaching without literalizing the examples of trees, mountains, or waves obeying.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the manner of Jacob's teaching.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The examples of obedient trees, mountains, and waves are described as power available through faith, not as a narrated event occurring now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a miracle or command affecting trees, mountains, or waves in this scene.

title: The Lord's mysteries
summary: Jacob teaches that the Lord's works are marvelous and his ways cannot all be discovered by man, then reasons that the power by which God created the earth and man allows him to command his creation.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says the Lord's works are great and marvelous, his mysteries unsearchable, and no one knows his ways unless they are revealed.
Jacob says man and the earth came to be by the power of God's word, and asks why God could not command the earth according to his will.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown teaching; no creation event need be depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and whether Jacob is addressing listeners.

narration.text: despise not the revelations of God
by the power of his word man came upon the face of the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The creation is recounted as teaching, not as a present-tense visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God or a creation scene; no appearance is described.

title: Take counsel from the Lord
summary: Jacob counsels his brethren not to counsel the Lord but to take counsel from him, teaching that the Lord counsels in wisdom, justice, and mercy.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob tells his brethren not to counsel the Lord but to take counsel from him.
Jacob says the Lord counsels in wisdom, justice, and great mercy over all his works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown teaching his brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and number of the brethren and the setting.

narration.text: seek not to counsel the Lord
he counseleth in wisdom, and in justice, and in great mercy

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific exchange, audience size, or reaction.

title: Reconciliation through Christ
summary: Jacob urges his beloved brethren to be reconciled to God through Christ's atonement, with faith and hope in Christ, and asks why they should not speak of the atonement and gain knowledge of Christ, resurrection, and the world to come.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob urges his beloved brethren to be reconciled to God through the atonement of Christ, his Only Begotten Son.
Jacob says they may obtain a resurrection and be presented as Christ's first-fruits unto God, having faith and good hope in him before his manifestation in the flesh.
Jacob asks why they should not speak of Christ's atonement and attain knowledge of him, resurrection, and the world to come.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, audience, and Jacob's physical posture.

narration.text: be reconciled unto him through the atonement of Christ
why not speak of the atonement of Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Christ's future manifestation in the flesh is referred to but not shown.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ's manifestation as occurring in this scene.

title: Plain prophecy
summary: Jacob teaches that the Spirit speaks truth plainly for salvation and that God also spoke to ancient prophets. He says the Jews rejected plain words and prophets, looked beyond the mark, and stumbled.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says prophecy should be given to men's understanding, the Spirit speaks truth, and these things are manifested plainly for salvation.
Jacob says God also spoke these things to prophets of old.
Jacob says the Jews despised plain words, killed prophets, and sought things they could not understand; their blindness came by looking beyond the mark, and they stumbled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown teaching; references to ancient prophets and the Jews are reported teachings, not necessarily present figures.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the historical prophets and the Jews, and the setting of Jacob's teaching.

narration.text: the Spirit speaketh the truth and lieth not
they despised the words of plainness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Looking beyond the mark” is figurative language, not a literal visual action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the killing of prophets as a present event.
Do not depict the metaphorical mark as a literal object or target.

title: The rejected stone
summary: Jacob says the Spirit leads him to prophesy that the Jews will reject the stone on which they might build safely. According to scripture, that stone will become the only sure foundation, and he asks how they can build on it after rejecting it.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says the Spirit leads him to prophesy that the Jews will reject the stone on which they might build with a safe foundation.
Jacob says the stone will become the great, last, and only sure foundation on which the Jews can build.
Jacob asks how those who have rejected the sure foundation can build upon it so it becomes the head of their corner.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown teaching; the stone and foundation language may remain verbal and nonliteral.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal stone or building, and the audience's appearance.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Stone, foundation, and corner language is figurative teaching, not a narrated construction scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the Jews rejecting a literal stone or building a structure.

title: Jacob prepares to unfold a mystery
summary: Jacob says he will unfold the mystery to his beloved brethren, if he is not shaken from firmness in the Spirit and does not stumble because of his great anxiety for them.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says he will unfold a mystery to his beloved brethren, if he is not shaken from firmness in the Spirit or stumble because of his over-anxiety for them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown continuing his teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Jacob's expression, posture, audience, and setting.

narration.text: I will unfold this mystery unto you

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The mystery's explanation is not included in this chapter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not reveal or depict the mystery's later explanation.
